rule: Go: package-path-qualified: `example.com/m/pkg.Type#Method`, `pkg.Func`; closures `pkg.F$1`. | Free function: its name (with the language's module qualifier where it has one). | high: the callee is a function/method/constructor defined in the scanned source (the tool matched it to a definition). medium: the callee is named statically (Type.m(), module.f(), an import, `self.m()` inherited from a base outside the scan, an external library type) but is not defined in the scan.
notes: The root package of module example.com/m has path example.com/m, so its functions are example.com/m.f (Go note: package-path-qualified). The aliased import u "example.com/m/util" resolves to the defining package (C1: every reference uses the definition's one ID). Standard-library packages are qualified by their import path (path/filepath.Base), medium because they are not defined in the scan. Package functions use call_type direct. The import declarations are not calls (C3: module dependency).
